skill.name: longbridge-technical
skill.description: Analyze stocks with candlestick, indicator, Ichimoku, harmonic, Elliott Wave, Chan Theory, Smart Money, and Turtle Trading frameworks using Longbridge OHLCV data.
skill.summary: Generate structured technical analysis and risk-aware trading signals from Longbridge market data.
skill.author: longbridge

security_audit.summary: Most alerts are false positives from Markdown backticks, calculations, multilingual text, and conventional device redirection. Package installation and predictable temporary paths present genuine risks. Missing relative scripts and unquoted symbol placeholders add command-execution exposure.

remediation.issue: Predictable shared temporary file paths permit tampering, data disclosure, or symlink attacks.
remediation.suggestion: Create unique temporary files with restrictive permissions and delete them after analysis.

remediation.issue: Unpinned pip installation instructions expose users to dependency and package-index compromise.
remediation.suggestion: Declare reviewed, pinned dependencies with hashes and require explicit approval before installation.

remediation.issue: The skill executes a relative signal engine that is absent from the package.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle and review the script, verify its integrity, and resolve it from the trusted skill directory.

remediation.issue: Shell examples interpolate symbols without validation or quoting.
remediation.suggestion: Allow only documented symbol characters and pass values as separate process arguments.

content.value_statement: Technical analysis often requires several methods and consistent data preparation. This skill applies nine structured frameworks to Longbridge OHLCV data and explains each result.
actual_capabilities: Fetch OHLCV data through the Longbridge CLI or an MCP fallback.
Recognize 15 classic candlestick patterns with trend and volume confirmation.
Calculate RSI, MACD, EMA, Bollinger Bands, ADX, OBV, and KDJ signals.
Evaluate Ichimoku, harmonic, Elliott Wave, Chan Theory, and Smart Money structures.
Generate Turtle breakouts, ATR, Unit sizing, stop levels, and add-on levels.
Produce reports in English, Simplified Chinese, or Traditional Chinese.
limitations: The workflows require sufficient OHLCV history, often between 60 and 300 bars.
Some frameworks require external Python packages, and the advanced Elliott script is not included.
Technical signals are probabilistic and do not replace licensed financial advice.
Account sizing requires authorized account access or a user-provided account value.

use_cases.title: Review a Stock
use_cases.description: Combine indicators and chart structures into one dated analysis with clear support, resistance, and invalidation conditions.

use_cases.title: Compare Technical Methods
use_cases.description: Check whether candlestick, Ichimoku, Elliott Wave, and momentum signals agree or conflict.

use_cases.title: Teach Rule-Based Trading
use_cases.description: Demonstrate Turtle breakouts, ATR risk, Unit sizing, stops, and market-specific constraints with worked examples.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Core Indicators
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze AAPL.US with RSI, MACD, EMA, and Bollinger Bands using 200 daily candles. Explain every signal in plain English.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Frameworks
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze 700.HK with candlestick and Ichimoku methods. Identify agreement, conflicts, invalidation levels, and the data date.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Market Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate NVDA.US with Elliott Wave and Smart Money Concepts. Present alternate counts, momentum confirmation, key zones, and uncertainty.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Turtle Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan my authorized watchlist for Turtle System 1 and System 2 signals. Calculate ATR and Unit sizing from a $100,000 account value.

output_examples.output: Trend: bullish but extended. MACD supports momentum, RSI is near overbought, and price is above both major moving averages.

output_examples.input: Calculate a Turtle Unit for a $100,000 account when N is $2.50.
output_examples.output: One Unit is 400 shares. A stop placed 2N from entry risks about $2,000, or 2% of account value.

output_examples.input: Compare two possible Elliott Wave counts.
output_examples.output: The primary count suggests a late impulse, while the alternate count remains corrective. Conflicting momentum keeps the structure unconfirmed.

best_practices: Confirm the symbol and market suffix before requesting data.
State the timeframe, bar count, and data cutoff in every analysis.
Compare independent signals and preserve uncertainty when frameworks disagree.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a single indicator as a guaranteed trade signal.
Do not install packages or read account data without explicit user approval.
Do not provide position sizes when account value or ATR data is missing.

faq.question: What data does this skill need?
faq.answer: It needs OHLCV history from Longbridge. Required history varies by framework and can reach 300 daily bars.

faq.question: Can this skill place trades?
faq.answer: No. It analyzes data and produces signals, levels, and position-sizing references.

faq.question: Which frameworks are supported?
faq.answer: It covers candlesticks, Ichimoku, indicators, harmonics, Elliott Wave, Chan Theory, Smart Money Concepts, and Turtle Trading.

faq.question: Does it access my account?
faq.answer: Only Turtle sizing workflows may request authorized assets, positions, watchlists, or order history. You can provide account values manually.

faq.question: Are extra packages required?
faq.answer: Chan Theory and Smart Money workflows require third-party Python packages. Review and approve dependencies before installation.

faq.question: Are the signals reliable?
faq.answer: Signals depend on historical data and model assumptions. They can conflict, fail in changing markets, and do not guarantee returns.
